topic: Pay Off Credit Cards or Other High Interest Debt
subtopic: Pay Off Credit Cards or Other High Interest Debt
source_evidence: If you’ve got unpaid balances on several credit cards, you should first pay down the card that charges the highest rate. Pay as much as you can toward that debt each month until your balance is once again zero, while still paying the minimum on your other cards. The same advice goes for any other high-interest debt (about 8% or above), which does not offer any tax advantages.
answer: When you have balances on multiple credit cards, prioritize paying down the card with the highest interest rate. Put as much as you can toward that balance while continuing to make at least the minimum payments on your other cards. After the highest-rate balance is paid off, you can focus on the next one. The source gives similar guidance for other high-interest debt, about 8% or above, when it offers no tax advantages.
